summary: Salak Airport (MVR) serves Maroua, the capital of Cameroon's Far North Region, providing a vital air link between the remote northern Sahel zone and the rest of the country. Situated at an elevation in the semi-arid savanna near the borders with Chad and Nigeria, it is the primary gateway for travelers heading to Waza National Park and surrounding wildlife reserves. The airport handles primarily domestic routes connecting to Douala and Yaoundé, supporting regional commerce and humanitarian operations in the Lake Chad basin.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate from Salak Airport?
A: The airport is mainly served by domestic Cameroonian carriers operating flights to Douala and Yaoundé, with schedules that can vary seasonally.

Q: Is Salak Airport an international airport?
A: While classified as a medium-sized airport with customs facilities, international commercial service is limited; most traffic is domestic.

Q: How far is the airport from Maroua city center?
A: The airport is located a short drive from central Maroua, typically around 10-15 minutes by road depending on traffic.

Q: Are there flights available year-round?
A: Yes, though schedules may be affected during the rainy season (roughly June-September) due to weather conditions in the region.
transport_tips: Taxis and motorbike taxis are the most common ways to reach central Maroua from Salak Airport; negotiate fares in advance as meters are rarely used. Car hire with a driver is recommended for travelers continuing onward to Waza National Park or other remote destinations in the Far North. Road conditions can be poor during the rainy season, so plan extra travel time when connecting onward by ground transport.
local_tip: Bring plenty of drinking water and arrive with cash in CFA francs, as the airport terminal has limited amenities and no reliable ATM on-site.
